target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — published specimen/distribution records; Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index and Balcones Canyonlands Preserve list; Bexar — documented native occurrence in San Antonio/Bexar County and central Texas county distribution.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaves and bracts. Bracted passionflower has broad 2–3-lobed 'cowboy-hat' leaves, small greenish-yellow flowers with conspicuous floral bracts, and a delicate corona. Tiny nectaries occur on the lower leaf surface.
diagnostic_traits: leaves broader than long, usually 2–3 rounded lobes
outer corona filaments long and sinuous
nectaries present on abaxial leaf surface

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. lutea lacks floral bracts and abaxial leaf nectaries and has smaller flowers. P. foetida is much hairier, foul-smelling when rubbed, and has a conspicuous cage of finely divided involucral bracts around the flower/fruit.
